PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality defensive franchise with strong brand portfolio, consistent cash generation, and a 70-year dividend increase streak. However, near-term fundamentals show sequential deceleration: Q3 FY2026 revenue declined QoQ (-4.4%) and EPS fell (-8.4%), with operating cash flow also declining QoQ (-18.6%). YoY growth remains positive but modest (revenue +7.4%, EPS +5.8%). The company faces a ~$400M after-tax tariff headwind and ~$1B oil-driven cost spike concentrated in the upcoming Q4 report (July 29), with management guiding to the low end of the $6.83-$7.09 core EPS range. Valuation at 23.8x P/E sits mid-range of its 1-year window (21.7-26.3x), neither cheap nor expensive. The upcoming Q4 earnings report on July 29 is a near-term catalyst — if the trough quarter is confirmed and FY2027 guidance shows reacceleration to ~8% EPS growth, the stock could re-rate. However, private-label pressure in key categories (diapers, tissue), tariff exposure, and the need to rebuild volume momentum after years of price-led growth temper enthusiasm. The score reflects a solid but not exceptional fundamental position with modest upside if the earnings trough is confirmed.

sources_cited.excerpt: Procter & Gamble has announced its 70th consecutive dividend increase, with a current dividend yield of 2.9% and annual dividend of $4.26 per share

Procter & Gamble Earnings Are Coming July 29. The Trough Quarter May Already Be Priced In. Normalized EPS is set to fall 4% year-over-year this fiscal fourth quarter before reaccelerating to 8% growth by June 2027

Procter & Gamble is absorbing roughly $400 million in after-tax tariff costs in fiscal 2026, alongside commodity headwinds and higher reinvestment spending. Core gross margin compressed 100 basis points last quarter

CFO Andre Schulten: We now expect a headwind of approximately $150 million after tax for the fiscal from a combination of commodity-linked cost inflation, feedstock exposures and logistics disruptions. Nearly all of that cost lands in the fiscal fourth quarter
Analysts expect PG to report an adjusted EPS of $1.42, down 4.1% from $1.48 in the year-ago quarter. However, it has surpassed Wall Street's earnings estimates in each of the last four quarters
Procter & Gamble's tariff-exposed supply chain, high debt and slower forecast growth could be masking a more fragile income story than it appears
